text: This one's yours to actually do — in a free Fabric trial or your own sandbox tenant. Five tasks, one per chapter, start to finish.

Structure first: a workspace, assigned to a domain, with roles you actually understand. Then land real data — a Lakehouse, load to tables, and a look at where OneLake security would restrict a folder. Then protect it: a sensitivity label, and a read-through of a real row-level security role if your tenant has one.

Make it discoverable — find it in the OneLake catalog, set it Promoted, and see what happens when you try Certified without authorization. Then close the loop: open Manage permissions, see who can Build right now, and write out what a real request-access flow should say.

Five questions, about the one item you built: which domain and who has which role, where the data actually lives, what label it carries, whether it's endorsed, and who can build against it right now. Answer all five without hunting, and you've internalized the course.

Congratulations — Chapter 1's tenant structure, all the way through a certified, permissioned, cataloged semantic model feeding an enterprise Purview catalog. The Data Governance path continues next with Databricks Unity Catalog Governance — the same instincts, applied to Databricks' own catalog and lineage tooling.
